**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind imported payments to the subscription's enrollment**

When a participant has multiple active enrollments, these independent ordered lookups can select an enrollment different from the one referenced by the selected active subscription—for example, an older enrollment may remain active after its subscription was cancelled. The `manual_payments` schema validates the subscription and enrollment with separate foreign keys, so the insert succeeds and silently attributes the imported payment to inconsistent billing/enrollment records. Derive `enrollment_id` from the selected subscription (or constrain the enrollment lookup to that subscription) instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 2ecf785587e340328e0922db17230398711adfa2, published on current head c757f32748bbd463891584c616b13ff0f8805d38. The selected active subscription now supplies enrollment_id; the subsequent lookup requires that exact enrollment, the same tenant/participant and active status. It cannot fall back to an older active enrollment.

The strengthened runtime regression failed before the fix with the exact wrong-enrollment UUID scenario (older active enrollment with a cancelled subscription, newer active subscription bound to another enrollment). It now passes and also proves that an inactive linked enrollment is rejected without an imported payment. Existing participant isolation and unprocessed payment rollback remain covered.

Migration 148 remains byte-identical. CLI-generated forward-only migration 149 (20260913182211) contains this correction. All 464 units, typecheck/build/packaging/audits and all thirteen database suites pass on both the canonical 147→149 upgrade and secure-default 149 fresh install. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-09-13-sql-lint-pre-v42/review-closure-validation.json and SQL-LINT-FASE-0.2-REPORT.md.
